Apollo Research is an AI safety organization. We specialize in auditing high-risk failure modes, particularly deceptive alignment, in large AI models. Our primary objective is to minimize catastrophic risks associated with advanced AI systems that may exhibit deceptive behavior, where misaligned models appear aligned in order to pursue their own objectives.

Our approach involves conducting fundamental research on interpretability and behavioral model evaluations, which we then use to audit real-world models. ## About

Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permis

properties.name: Covenant AI
properties.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

properties.name: Sodium
properties.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

CAIRA is a governed, evidence-anchored AI research engine built for organisations that need accuracy, traceability, and domain integrity. Earlier versions, CairAssist and Cairity proved that teams wanted more than structured prompting and clean document generation. They needed a system that could understand scientific complexity, maintain provenance, and produce outputs that meet clinical, policy, and publication-grade standards.

That evolution led to SuperNova, CAIRA’s federated small-language-model engine engineered specifically for healthcare, science, and regulatory work. SuperNova operates on the Maya governance layer, which enforces reasoning discipline, source verification, and auditability across every interaction. Instead of probabilistic answers, it delivers accountable intelligence - structured, explainable, and compliant.

One of CAIRA’s most significant advances is its Microsoft Azure-enabled inclusion interface, powered by the Maya Voice Integration layer. Users can now move fluidly between typing, speaking, and conversational reasoning without losing context or structure. A clinician can draft part of a summary in text, switch to voice to refine analysis, then return to written mode, all while CAIRA maintains the evidence chain, citations, and regulatory alignment. This multimodal and multilingual continuity makes the system accessible to busy researchers, multilingual teams, and people who benefit from more natural modes of interaction.

Today, CAIRA supports clinical research groups, med-tech strategy teams, public-health organisations, and policy units. It produces literature reviews, white papers, regulatory briefs, grant frameworks, and presentation-ready outputs with precision and verifiable sourcing.

CAIRA generates new innovation and works for bespoke needs. It is not a chatbot; it is a governed intelligence platform designed for environments where trust, accuracy, and accountability are non-negotiable.

entity.name: Covenant AI
entity.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

entity.name: Insignytics 2.0
entity.description:
Insignytics 2.0 is building LeapFrog, an AI runtime control plane for enterprises moving AI agents from pilots into production.

Enterprise AI is shifting from chat to execution. That changes the problem for CTOs, CIOs, and governance leaders. AI agents cannot act inside customer data, approvals, financial workflows, healthcare systems, or core operations unless actions are governed, permissioned, traceable, and controllable before execution.

Today, this is often handled through governance documents, manual approvals, custom integrations, platform-specific controls, and scattered logs. That may work during pilots, but it breaks when multiple agents, models, teams, workflows, and enterprise systems are involved.

LeapFrog sits between AI agents and enterprise systems. It checks actions before execution, enforces permissions and policies, supports human approval where needed, and creates a clear audit trail for production workflows.

Insignytics brings together enterprise GTM experience and deep middleware, integration, and platform architecture experience to solve this production-control gap.

LeapFrog is designed to give CTOs a governed path from AI pilots to production workflows where actions can be controlled and ROI can be measured.

entity.name: Sodium
entity.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

entity.name: Cognitive AI Research & Application
entity.description:
CAIRA is a governed, evidence-anchored AI research engine built for organisations that need accuracy, traceability, and domain integrity. Earlier versions, CairAssist and Cairity proved that teams wanted more than structured prompting and clean document generation. They needed a system that could understand scientific complexity, maintain provenance, and produce outputs that meet clinical, policy, and publication-grade standards.

That evolution led to SuperNova, CAIRA’s federated small-language-model engine engineered specifically for healthcare, science, and regulatory work. SuperNova operates on the Maya governance layer, which enforces reasoning discipline, source verification, and auditability across every interaction. Instead of probabilistic answers, it delivers accountable intelligence - structured, explainable, and compliant.

One of CAIRA’s most significant advances is its Microsoft Azure-enabled inclusion interface, powered by the Maya Voice Integration layer. Users can now move fluidly between typing, speaking, and conversational reasoning without losing context or structure. A clinician can draft part of a summary in text, switch to voice to refine analysis, then return to written mode, all while CAIRA maintains the evidence chain, citations, and regulatory alignment. This multimodal and multilingual continuity makes the system accessible to busy researchers, multilingual teams, and people who benefit from more natural modes of interaction.

Today, CAIRA supports clinical research groups, med-tech strategy teams, public-health organisations, and policy units. It produces literature reviews, white papers, regulatory briefs, grant frameworks, and presentation-ready outputs with precision and verifiable sourcing.

CAIRA generates new innovation and works for bespoke needs. It is not a chatbot; it is a governed intelligence platform designed for environments where trust, accuracy, and accountability are non-negotiable.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

Apollo Research is an AI safety organization. We specialize in auditing high-risk failure modes, particularly deceptive alignment, in large AI models. Our primary objective is to minimize catastrophic risks associated with advanced AI systems that may exhibit deceptive behavior, where misaligned models appear aligned in order to pursue their own objectives.

Our approach involves conducting fundamental research on interpretability and behavioral model evaluations, which we then use to audit real-world models. properties.name: Sodium
properties.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

## About

Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permis

properties.name: Covenant AI
properties.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

properties.name: Cognitive AI Research & Application
properties.description:
CAIRA is a governed, evidence-anchored AI research engine built for organisations that need accuracy, traceability, and domain integrity. Earlier versions, CairAssist and Cairity proved that teams wanted more than structured prompting and clean document generation. They needed a system that could understand scientific complexity, maintain provenance, and produce outputs that meet clinical, policy, and publication-grade standards.

That evolution led to SuperNova, CAIRA’s federated small-language-model engine engineered specifically for healthcare, science, and regulatory work. SuperNova operates on the Maya governance layer, which enforces reasoning discipline, source verification, and auditability across every interaction. Instead of probabilistic answers, it delivers accountable intelligence - structured, explainable, and compliant.

One of CAIRA’s most significant advances is its Microsoft Azure-enabled inclusion interface, powered by the Maya Voice Integration layer. Users can now move fluidly between typing, speaking, and conversational reasoning without losing context or structure. A clinician can draft part of a summary in text, switch to voice to refine analysis, then return to written mode, all while CAIRA maintains the evidence chain, citations, and regulatory alignment. This multimodal and multilingual continuity makes the system accessible to busy researchers, multilingual teams, and people who benefit from more natural modes of interaction.

Today, CAIRA supports clinical research groups, med-tech strategy teams, public-health organisations, and policy units. It produces literature reviews, white papers, regulatory briefs, grant frameworks, and presentation-ready outputs with precision and verifiable sourcing.

CAIRA generates new innovation and works for bespoke needs. It is not a chatbot; it is a governed intelligence platform designed for environments where trust, accuracy, and accountability are non-negotiable.

entity.name: Cohere Labs
entity.description:
Who we are
Cohere Labs is Cohere's research lab that seeks to solve complex machine learning problems. We support fundamental research that explores the unknown, and are focused on creating more points of entry into machine learning research.

Our community is a space where researchers, engineers, linguists, social scientists and lifelong learners connect and collaborate with each other. We come together from all over the world and welcome you whether you are a mentor, dropout, just getting started, PhD, masters, undergraduate, unaffiliated, industry, academic or not really sure. We are excited to support community-driven research and to be shaped by our members' interests. 

Where we’ve come from
In 2017, a team of friends, classmates, and engineers started a distributed research collaboration, with a focus on creating a medium for early-career AI enthusiasts to engage with experienced researchers – they called it “for.ai.” Two of those co-founding members, Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang, later went on to co-found Cohere, and many of the founding members went on to do exciting things (pursuing PhDs, working at industry and academic labs). 

At the time, For AI was one of the first community-driven research groups to support independent researchers around the world. Today, Cohere is proud to reintroduce For AI as Cohere Labs, a dedicated research lab and community for exploring the unknown, together.

The U.S. Space Force (USSF) is a new branch of the Armed Forces, established on December 20, 2019 with enactment of the Fiscal Year 2020 National Defense Authorization Act. The USSF was established within the Department of the Air Force, meaning the Secretary of the Air Force has overall responsibility for the USSF, under the guidance and direction of the Secretary of Defense. Additionally, a four-star general known as the Chief of Space Operations (CSO) serves as the senior military member of the USSF. The CSO is a full member of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. 

Mission 

The USSF is a military service that organizes, trains, and equips space forces in order to protect U.S. and allied interests in space and to provide space capabilities to the joint force. USSF responsibilities include developing military space professionals, acquiring military space systems, maturing the military doctrine for space power, and organizing space forces to present to our Combatant Commands.

Diversity is one of the hallmarks that defines us, and we draw strength from it as many of our residents come from the Caribbean and Central and South America. In fact, 70% of our population is Hispanic or Latino.

In 2016, the City of Miami was chosen along with the City of Miami Beach and Miami-Dade County as regional partners to join 100 Resilient Cities’ (100RC) global network which was founded by the Rockefeller Foundation. Miami is a Future City and as such, the city is addressing rising seas and climate concerns. 

City voters approved the Miami Forever Bond in November 2017 and the initial phase of the program was launched in December of 2018. The funding is earmarked for five key categories, including $192M allocated to mitigate the most severe current and future flood risks and vulnerability through strategic infrastructure investments. Some of the projects included are tidal backflow prevention valves, raised roads, and stormwater pumps to keep our streets dry and seawalls to protect our neighborhoods. The City is actively cultivating public and private partnerships in advancing its ambitious climate resilience strategy, which also includes non-infrastructure measures such as land use planning, building codes and hurricane preparedness.

entity.name: Sodium
entity.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

entity.name: Covenant AI
entity.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

entity.name: Cognitive AI Research & Application
entity.description:
CAIRA is a governed, evidence-anchored AI research engine built for organisations that need accuracy, traceability, and domain integrity. Earlier versions, CairAssist and Cairity proved that teams wanted more than structured prompting and clean document generation. They needed a system that could understand scientific complexity, maintain provenance, and produce outputs that meet clinical, policy, and publication-grade standards.

That evolution led to SuperNova, CAIRA’s federated small-language-model engine engineered specifically for healthcare, science, and regulatory work. SuperNova operates on the Maya governance layer, which enforces reasoning discipline, source verification, and auditability across every interaction. Instead of probabilistic answers, it delivers accountable intelligence - structured, explainable, and compliant.

One of CAIRA’s most significant advances is its Microsoft Azure-enabled inclusion interface, powered by the Maya Voice Integration layer. Users can now move fluidly between typing, speaking, and conversational reasoning without losing context or structure. A clinician can draft part of a summary in text, switch to voice to refine analysis, then return to written mode, all while CAIRA maintains the evidence chain, citations, and regulatory alignment. This multimodal and multilingual continuity makes the system accessible to busy researchers, multilingual teams, and people who benefit from more natural modes of interaction.

Today, CAIRA supports clinical research groups, med-tech strategy teams, public-health organisations, and policy units. It produces literature reviews, white papers, regulatory briefs, grant frameworks, and presentation-ready outputs with precision and verifiable sourcing.

CAIRA generates new innovation and works for bespoke needs. It is not a chatbot; it is a governed intelligence platform designed for environments where trust, accuracy, and accountability are non-negotiable.

Intelligence Cubed solves this by turning product usage data into proprietary training assets and enabling companies to fine-tune, evaluate, deploy, and improve their own models over time.

Our platform helps teams collect, clean, label, approve, version, and evaluate high-quality training data from conversations, workflows, expert edits, user feedback, and business outcomes. Companies can then fine-tune owned models from approved behavior data, compare model versions, measure quality, latency, cost, and brand consistency, and deploy the best-performing models into production.

Beyond fine-tuning, Intelligence Cubed provides the evaluation, routing, deployment, and feedback-loop infrastructure needed to operate models continuously. We believe the future of enterprise AI will not be defined by static prompts or isolated APIs, but by companies that build compounding model advantages through proprietary data, fine-tuned behavior, and continuous improvement.

B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of

    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label

  extras: {"url": "https://na.ai/", "entity": {"name": "Sodium", "foundedYear": null, "description": "Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. Who we are
Cohere Labs is Cohere's research lab that seeks to solve complex machine learning problems. We support fundamental research that explores the unknown, and are focused on creating more points of entry into machine learning research.

Our community is a space where researchers, engineers, linguists, social scientists and lifelong learners connect and collaborate with each other. We come together from all over the world and welcome you whether you are a mentor, dropout, just getting started, PhD, masters, undergraduate, unaffiliated, industry, academic or not really sure. We are excited to support community-driven research and to be shaped by our members' interests. 

Where we’ve come from
In 2017, a team of friends, classmates, and engineers started a distributed research collaboration, with a focus on creating a medium for early-career AI enthusiasts to engage with experienced researchers – they called it “for.ai.” Two of those co-founding members, Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang, later went on to co-found Cohere, and many of the founding members went on to do exciting things (pursuing PhDs, working at industry and academic labs). 

At the time, For AI was one of the first community-driven research groups to support independent researchers around the world. Today, Cohere is proud to reintroduce For AI as Cohere Labs, a dedicated research lab and community for exploring the unknown, together.

Our Principles
Every tool we build is open source
Every pilot includes independent third-party evaluation
Every dollar raised supports program engineering or pilot cohorts at partner institutions

US AI4Good Inc is a registered 501(c)(3) public charity.

Competitor Swim was established with the introduction of the Non-Turb™ Racing Lane at the 1968 Summer Olympics. This lane set a standard in the industry, as it was the first flexible swim lane to effectively dissipate turbulent water while simultaneously creating a wave control barrier for optimum racing conditions.

The Competitor Racing Lane eventually evolved into today’s Gold Medal Racing Lane™ whose patented technology was introduced at the 1992 Summer Olympic Games in Barcelona, Spain. Competitor’s Gold Medal Racing Lane™ has proudly been the choice of 9 of the past 12 Olympic Games, most recently at the 2012 London Games.

Closer to home, Competitor Racing Lanes have been used in countless Men’s & Women’s Championships, numerous high school State Championships and USA Swimming events across the country.

Every customer is different. Every pool is different. We believe each and every lane should be built specifically for each customer. All of our lanes are custom built by hand with pride, passion, and expertise. We take great pride in the fact that all Competitor Racing Lanes are manufactured and assembled PROUDLY in AMERICA.

Competitor Swim’s line of products also includes stor lane reels, pace clocks, backstroke flags and the Original Swedish Goggle. We bring the same passion and commitment to each of these swimming accessories, as we do to our lanes and the sport of swimming.

## About

Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permis

properties.name: Covenant AI
properties.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

properties.name: Sodium
properties.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

entity.name: Cohere Labs
entity.description:
Who we are
Cohere Labs is Cohere's research lab that seeks to solve complex machine learning problems. We support fundamental research that explores the unknown, and are focused on creating more points of entry into machine learning research.

Our community is a space where researchers, engineers, linguists, social scientists and lifelong learners connect and collaborate with each other. We come together from all over the world and welcome you whether you are a mentor, dropout, just getting started, PhD, masters, undergraduate, unaffiliated, industry, academic or not really sure. We are excited to support community-driven research and to be shaped by our members' interests. 

Where we’ve come from
In 2017, a team of friends, classmates, and engineers started a distributed research collaboration, with a focus on creating a medium for early-career AI enthusiasts to engage with experienced researchers – they called it “for.ai.” Two of those co-founding members, Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang, later went on to co-found Cohere, and many of the founding members went on to do exciting things (pursuing PhDs, working at industry and academic labs). 

At the time, For AI was one of the first community-driven research groups to support independent researchers around the world. Today, Cohere is proud to reintroduce For AI as Cohere Labs, a dedicated research lab and community for exploring the unknown, together.

entity.name: Intelligence Cubed i³
entity.description:
Intelligence Cubed is building intelligence infrastructure that helps companies move from prompt-wrapper AI products to owned, fine-tuned model systems.

Most enterprise AI products today rely on generic foundation model APIs and prompt engineering, which makes it difficult for companies to own their model behavior, preserve domain expertise, reduce inference cost, or continuously improve from real user interactions. Intelligence Cubed solves this by turning product usage data into proprietary training assets and enabling companies to fine-tune, evaluate, deploy, and improve their own models over time.

Our platform helps teams collect, clean, label, approve, version, and evaluate high-quality training data from conversations, workflows, expert edits, user feedback, and business outcomes. Companies can then fine-tune owned models from approved behavior data, compare model versions, measure quality, latency, cost, and brand consistency, and deploy the best-performing models into production.

Beyond fine-tuning, Intelligence Cubed provides the evaluation, routing, deployment, and feedback-loop infrastructure needed to operate models continuously. We believe the future of enterprise AI will not be defined by static prompts or isolated APIs, but by companies that build compounding model advantages through proprietary data, fine-tuned behavior, and continuous improvement.

Competitor Swim was established with the introduction of the Non-Turb™ Racing Lane at the 1968 Summer Olympics. This lane set a standard in the industry, as it was the first flexible swim lane to effectively dissipate turbulent water while simultaneously creating a wave control barrier for optimum racing conditions.

The Competitor Racing Lane eventually evolved into today’s Gold Medal Racing Lane™ whose patented technology was introduced at the 1992 Summer Olympic Games in Barcelona, Spain. Competitor’s Gold Medal Racing Lane™ has proudly been the choice of 9 of the past 12 Olympic Games, most recently at the 2012 London Games.

Closer to home, Competitor Racing Lanes have been used in countless Men’s & Women’s Championships, numerous high school State Championships and USA Swimming events across the country.

Every customer is different. Every pool is different. We believe each and every lane should be built specifically for each customer. All of our lanes are custom built by hand with pride, passion, and expertise. We take great pride in the fact that all Competitor Racing Lanes are manufactured and assembled PROUDLY in AMERICA.

Competitor Swim’s line of products also includes stor lane reels, pace clocks, backstroke flags and the Original Swedish Goggle. We bring the same passion and commitment to each of these swimming accessories, as we do to our lanes and the sport of swimming.

entity.name: Covenant AI
entity.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

entity.name: Sodium
entity.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.
